rows.source: Masu gabatar da kara na tarayya na neman hukuncin kisa na kisa ga dan ta’adda NYC
rows.output: The federal prosecutors are seeking the death penalty for the NYC bomber.
rows.reference: Federal prosecutors seeking rare death penalty for NYC terror attack suspect

rows.source: Masu gabatar da kara na tarayya a birnin New York suna neman hukuncin kisa ga Sayfullo Saipov, wanda ake zargin a harin da ya faru a birnin New York, wanda ya kashe mutane takwas - hukuncin da ba a yi ba a jihar don aikata laifukan tarayya tun shekara ta 1953.
rows.output: The federal prosecutors in New York are seeking the death penalty for Sayfullo Saipov, who is accused of the attack in New York City, which killed eight people - a sentence that has not been carried out in the state for federal crimes since 1953.
rows.reference: Federal prosecutors in New York are seeking the death penalty for Sayfullo Saipov, the suspect in the New York City terror attack that killed eight people -- a rare punishment that hasn't been carried out in the state for a federal crime since 1953.

rows.source: Saipov, mai shekaru 30, ya yi amfani da motoci mai hawa na gida domin gudanar da hare-haren kan hanyar machine da ta hanyar West Side Highway a Lower Manhattan, inda ya kaddamar akan masu tafiya a kafa da kekuna a hanyarsa a watan Oktoba.
rows.output: Saipov, 30, used a rental truck to carry out the attack on the West Side Highway in Lower Manhattan, targeting pedestrians and cyclists in his path in October.
rows.reference: Saipov, 30, allegedly used a Home Depot rental truck to carry out an attack on a bike path along the West Side Highway in Lower Manhattan, mowing down pedestrians and cyclist in his path on Oct.

rows.source: Don tabbatar da hukuncin kisa, masu gabatar da kara za su tabbatar da cewa Saipov "da gangan" ya kashe mutane takwas da "ganganci" ya jawo mummunan rauni a jiki, bisa ga sanarwar na neman hukuncin kisa, aka a yankin Kudancin Sabon Gundumar New York.
rows.output: To ensure the death penalty, the prosecution will prove that Saipov "intentionally" killed eight people and "intentionally" caused serious physical injury to others, according to the notice of the death penalty, in the Southern District of New York.
rows.reference: In order to justify a death sentence, prosecutors will have to prove that Saipov "intentionally" killed the eight victims and "intentionally" inflicted serious bodily injury, according to the notice of intent to seek the death penalty, filed in the Southern District of New York.

rows.source: Dukkan waɗanda nan la'akari su na da hukuncin kisa, bisa ga takardun kotu.
rows.output: All those considered are sentenced to death, according to court documents.
rows.reference: Both of those counts carry a possibly death sentence, according to the court document.

rows.source: Makonni bayan harin, babban kotun tarayya ta maka wa Saipov zarge-zarge 22 da suka hada da laifuffuka guda takwas na kisan kai don taimakon rashin gaskiya, yawanci sune masu gabatar da kara ke yi a laifukan shiryeyyen laifi, da kuma cajin tashin hankali da halakar da motoci.
rows.output: A few weeks after the attack, the Federal High Court indicted Saipov on 22 charges, including eight counts of terrorism for providing material support to a terrorist organization, most of which are typically brought by prosecutors in terrorism cases, and conspiracy to cause mass destruction and damage to vehicles.
rows.reference: Weeks after the attack, a federal grand jury slapped Saipov with a 22-count indictment that included eight charges of murder in aid of racketeering, typically used by federal prosecutors in organized crime cases, and a charge of violence and destruction of motor vehicles.

rows.source: Wannan harin ya bukaci "tsarawa mai mahimmanci da kaddamarwa," in ji masu gabatar da kara, inda ya bayyana irin yadda Saipov ya dauki shi a matsayin "mai mugunta, mummunan hali da kuma marar sa tausayi."
rows.output: This attack required "a high degree of planning and preparation," the prosecutors said, describing how Saipov took it on as "a cruel, despicable and inhumane act."
rows.reference: The attack required "substantial planning and premeditation," prosecutors said, describing the manner in which Saipov carried it out as "heinous, cruel and depraved."

rows.source: "Sayfullo Habibullaevic Saipov ya haifar da rauni, cuta, da hasara ga iyalai da abokai Diego Enrique Angelini, Nicholas Cleves, Ann-Laure Decadt, Darren Drake, Ariel Erlij, Hernan Ferruchi, Hernan Diego Mendoza, da Alejandro Damian Pagnucco," sanarwa na niyyar jihohi.
rows.output: "Sayfullo Habibullaevic Saipov ya haifar da rauni, cuta, da hasara ga iyalai da abokai Diego Enrique Angelini, Nicholas Cleves, Ann-Laure Decadt, Darren Drake, Ariel Erlij, Hernan Ferruchi, Hernan Diego Mendoza, da Alejandro Damian Pagnucco," sanarwa na niyyar jihohi.
rows.reference: "Sayfullo Habibullaevic Saipov caused injury, harm, and loss to the families and friends of Diego Enrique Angelini, Nicholas Cleves, Ann-Laure Decadt, Darren Drake, Ariel Erlij, Hernan Ferruchi, Hernan Diego Mendoza, and Alejandro Damian Pagnucco," the notice of intent states.

rows.source: Biyar daga cikin waɗanda aka kashe 'yan yawon bude ido daga Argentina
rows.output: Four of the victims were tourists from Argentina
rows.reference: Five of the victims were tourists from Argentina.

rows.source: An yi shekaru goma tun lokacin da yankin kudancin New York ya kaddamar da hukuncin kisa.
rows.output: Ten years have passed since the Southern District of New York issued its death penalty ruling.
rows.reference: It has been a decade since the Southern District of New York last prosecuted a death penalty case.

rows.source: Wanda aka gurfanar da shi, Khalid Barnes, an yanke masa hukunci ne game da kashe masu raba kwaya biyu, amma an yanke masa hukuncin kisa a watan Satumba na 2009.
rows.output: The defendant, Khalid Barnes, was convicted of the murders of two drug dealers, but sentenced to death in September 2009.
rows.reference: The defendant, Khalid Barnes, was convicted of murdering two drug suppliers but was ultimately sentenced to life in prison in September 2009.

rows.source: karshen a lokacin da aka yanke hukuncin kisa a tarayya New York a 1953 ga Julius da Ethel Rosenberg, ma'aurata bayan da aka yanke musu hukuncin kulla makirci don Tarayyar Soviet a lokacin Yakin Tsana shekaru biyu da suka gabata.
rows.output: The end of the era of capital punishment in the United States came in 1953 with the execution of Julius and Ethel Rosenberg, a married couple who were sentenced to death for espionage for the Soviet Union during the Cold War two years earlier.
rows.reference: The last time the death penalty was carried out in a New York federal case was in 1953 for Julius and Ethel Rosenberg, a married couple executed after they were convicted of conspiracy to commit espionage for the Soviet Union during the Cold War two years before.

rows.source: Dukansu Rosenbergs sun mutu ne ta hanyar kujerar lantarki ranar 19 ga Yuni, 1953.
rows.output: They both died of a heart attack on June 19, 1953.
rows.reference: Both Rosenbergs were both put to death by the electric chair on June 19, 1953.

rows.source: Saipov, dan kasar Uzbekistan, ya nuna rashin tausayi a cikin kwanaki da watanni bayan harin, bisa ga takardun kotu.
rows.output: Saipov, a citizen of Uzbekistan, showed no remorse in the days and months following the attack, according to court documents.
rows.reference: Saipov, a native of Uzbekistan, demonstrated a lack of remorse in the days and months following the attack, according to court documents.

rows.source: Ya bayyana wa masu binciken cewa ya jin daɗin abin da ya yi, 'yan sanda sun ce.
rows.output: He told the investigators that he enjoyed what he did, the police said.
rows.reference: He stated to investigators that he felt good about what he had done, police said.

rows.source: Saipov ya shaida wa hukumomin da cewa ya samu kwarin guiwa bayan gudanar da harin bayan ya duba bidiyon ISIS a wayarsa, bisa ga zargin.
rows.output: Saipov testified to the authorities that he was inspired to carry out the attack after watching an ISIS video on his phone, according to the allegations.
rows.reference: Saipov told authorities he was inspired to carry out the attack after watching ISIS videos on his phone, according to the indictment.

rows.source: Har ila yau, ya bukaci a nuna tutar Isis a cikin dakin asibiti, in ji 'yan sanda.
rows.output: In addition, he requested that the Isis flag be displayed in the hospital room, police said.
rows.reference: He also requested to display the ISIS flag in his hospital room, police said.

rows.source: Ya yi zargin ba shi da laifi ga tuhuma 22 na zargin.
rows.output: He pleaded not guilty to 22 counts of bribery.
rows.reference: He has pleaded not guilty to the 22-count indictment.

rows.source: David Patton, daya daga cikin masu kare hakkin jama'a na tarayya a jihar Saipov, ya ce su na da "takaici" tare da yanke shawara.
rows.output: David Patton, one of the federal defenders in the Saipov case, said they were "disappointed" with the ruling.
rows.reference: David Patton, one of the federal public defenders representing Saipov, said they are "obviously disappointed" with the prosecution's decision.

rows.source: "Mu na tsammanin shawarar da za a nemi hukuncin kisa maimakon karɓar laifin mai laifi zuwa rai a kurkuku ba tare da yiwuwar saki ba zai shawo kan matsalolin abubuwan da ke faruwa ga kowa da kowa", inji Patton.
rows.output: "We expect that the decision to seek the death penalty instead of accepting the guilty plea of the offender, who will be sentenced to life in prison without the possibility of parole, will address the problems that are occurring for everyone," said Patton.
rows.reference: "We think the decision to seek the death penalty rather than accepting a guilty plea to life in prison with no possibility of release will only prolong the trauma of these events for everyone involved," Patton said.

rows.source: Lauyoyi masu kare Saipov sun nemi masu gabatar da kara kada su nemi hukuncin kisa.
rows.output: The lawyers defending Saipov have requested the prosecution not to seek the death penalty.
rows.reference: Saipov's defense team had previously asked prosecutors not to seek the death penalty.

rows.source: Tory MP ya ce NIGEL FARAGE ya kamata a kula da tattaunawar Brexit
rows.output: Tory MP says NIGEL FARAGE should be held accountable for the Brexit talks
rows.reference: Tory MP says NIGEL FARAGE should be put in charge of Brexit negotiations

rows.output: Nigel Farage has vowed to cause chaos today during a Tory rally.

rows.source: Tsohon shugaban Ukip ya ce 'yan siyasar sun' ji zafi 'daga' yan kasuwa na Eurosceptics - kamar yadda daya daga cikin wakilai na Theresa May ta ba da shawara cewa ya kamata tayi la'akari da tattaunawar da EU.
rows.output: Former Ukip leader Nigel Farage said the party's politicians had "suffered pain" from the Eurosceptic business community - as one of Theresa May's representatives suggested she should consider talking to the EU.
rows.reference: The former Ukip leader said politicians had to 'feel the heat' from Eurosceptics - as one of Theresa May's own MPs suggested he should be in charge of negotiations with the EU.

rows.source: Wani mai goyon baya na baya-bayan nan, Peter Bone, ya shaida wa manema labaru a Birmingham cewa Birtaniya za ta fita daga yanzu idan Mr Farage ya zama Sakatare Brexit.
rows.output: A recent backer, Peter Bone, told reporters in Birmingham that Britain would now leave the EU if Mr. Farage became the Brexit Secretary.
rows.reference: Conservative backbencher Peter Bone told the march in Birmingham that the UK 'would have been out' by now if Mr Farage was Brexit Secretary.

rows.source: Amma ƙalubalen da Mrs May ta fuskanta wajen sulhu da ragamar da aka yi a tsakanin bangarori daban-daban da aka yi sun nuna cewa, Pro-Remain Tories na shiga cikin rashin amincewa da Brexit a birnin.
rows.output: But the challenges faced by Mrs May in negotiating the terms of the Brexit referendum, which was approved by a majority of voters, have shown that pro-Remain Tory MPs are in a state of disarray over the issue in the capital.
rows.reference: But the challenge Mrs May faces in reconciling her deeply divided ranks has been underlined by pro-Remain Tories joining a separate protest against Brexit in the city.

rows.source: Fremiya na fama da matsalolin kulawa da masu bincikenta sunyi shiri akan hanya a cikin hare-hare daga Brexiteers, Remainers da EU.

rows.source: Abokai sun dage cewa ta tura gaba tare da ƙoƙarina buga yarjejeniyar tare da Brussels duk da sakamakon - kuma ta tilasta yan Turai da Labour don su zabi tsakaninta da 'rudani'.
rows.output: Friends insisted that she push ahead with my efforts to sign a deal with Brussels despite the outcome - and force the Europeans and the Labour Party to choose between her and 'confusion'.
rows.reference: Allies insisted she will push ahead with trying to strike a deal with Brussels despite the backlash - and force Eurosceptics and Labour to choose between her package and 'chaos'.

rows.source: Mista Bone ya shaida wa kamfanin dillancin labaran AFP cewa, yana son 'duba' 'Masu binciken'.
rows.output: Mr. Bone told the news agency AFP that he wanted to "see" the "investigators".
rows.reference: Mr Bone told the Leave Means Leave rally in Solihull that he wanted to 'chuck Chequers'.

rows.output: They don't want to know who they wronged, who they will have to climb over to get power and control, that's what they want power and control, we won't give it to them.

rows.output: The Democrats, he said, are on a journey to "block and obstruct."

rows.source: Elee anya, abụ onye nke kachasị ọhụrụ n’ahịrị nke MP ndị Labour agwara na anabataghị - naanị maka ikwu uche anyị.
rows.output: I'm the most recent addition to the line of Labour MPs who have been told they're not welcome - just for speaking our minds.

rows.output: In my opinion, the moderation panel criticized me for questioning Jeremy Corbyn.

rows.source: Na mkpa nke iwu akụnụba obodo ziri ezi, nche obodo, yana Europe, n’ụzọ ọzọ otu nsogbu ndị Jeremy jiri na ekwenyeghị na ndị isi gara aga.
rows.output: In the need of a sound national economic policy, national security, and Europe, in other words, one problem that Jeremy disagreed with the previous leaders.
rows.reference: On the importance of a responsible economic policy, on national security, on Europe, ironically similar issues on which Jeremy disagreed with previous leaders.

rows.source: Ọkwa maka nzụkọ Nottingham East Labour na Fraịde kwuru na “anyị chọrọ nzụkọ ndị ahụ bụrụ nke dum ma mịpụta mkpụrụ.”
rows.output: The statement for the Nottingham East Labour meeting on Friday said, "We want the meetings to be full and fruitful."
rows.reference: The notice for the Nottingham East Labour meeting on Friday stated that "we want the meetings to be inclusive and productive."

rows.source: N’imirikiti afọ asatọ m ka MP Labour mpaghara ahụ, abalị Fraịde nzụkọ GC na abụkarị nke ahụ.
rows.output: In the past eight years, I have been the Labour MP for the area, and on Friday nights, the GC meeting is usually the one.
rows.reference: For most of my eight years as the local Labour MP, the Friday night GC meetings have been exactly that.

rows.source: Na mwute taa, ọ bụghị olu nke imirikiti nzụkọ yana ndọrọndọrọ “obi ọma, ume ala” ekwere na nkwa bụ ihe ndị echefugoro kemgbe ma ọ bụrụ, n’ezie, o bidoro ma ncha.
rows.output: Unfortunately, it is not the voice of the meeting that is heard, and the "good intentions, strong will" that were promised have been forgotten since, if at all, the soap opera began.
rows.reference: Sadly today, it is not the tone of many meetings and the promise of "kinder, gentler" politics has long been forgotten if, indeed, it ever began.

rows.source: Ọ bụ ihe pụtara ihie nke ukwuu na anaghị anabata nghọta dị iche iche na ndọrọndọrọ Labour, ọzọkwa a na ekpezi echiche ọ bụla ma a ga-anabata ya n’ọchịchị ndọrọndọrọ ahụ.
rows.output: It is a significant issue that the Labour Party does not accept different interpretations of its policies, and any opinion is not accepted in the party's leadership.
rows.reference: It has become increasingly apparent that differing views are not tolerated in the Labour party and every opinion is judged on whether it is acceptable to the party leadership.

rows.source: Nke a bidoro ozugbo Jeremy bụrụ onye isi, ndị ọrụ ibe m, ndị m chere na mụ na ha na ekekọrịta otu nghọta ndọrọndọrọ bidoro tụba anya na m ga-atụgharị ozugbo ma were ọnọdụ ndị m ga-agaghị ekwekọrịta na ya otu ọ bụla - ma ọ bụ na nchedo obodo ma ọ bụ otu ahịa EU.
rows.output: This began immediately after Jeremy became leader, my colleagues, with whom I had previously shared a common understanding of politics, started to look at me as someone who would have to be turned around and who would take on a position that I would not agree with on any issue - whether national security or the EU market.
rows.reference: This started shortly after Jeremy became leader, as colleagues with whom I had previously thought I shared a similar political outlook began expecting me to do a U-turn and take positions I would never have otherwise agreed with - whether on national security or the EU single market.

rows.source: Mgbe ọ bụla m kwuru okwu n’ọhaneze - ọ gaghị agbasata ihe m kwuru - a na enwe nkwụtọ dị ukwuu na esote ozugbo n’ebe mmerịkọta ọhaneze na akpọ maka mwepu, nkatọ ndọrọndọrọ nke etiti, na agwa m na m ekwesịghị ịnọ na ndọrọndọrọ Labour.
rows.output: Whenever I speak in public - it will not be repeated - there is a great deal of criticism that follows immediately in the media and in the call for my removal, the criticism of my centrality in the party, and my character that I should not be in the Labour Party.
rows.reference: Whenever I speak publicly - and it doesn't really matter what I say - there follows a tirade of abuse on social media calling for deselection, denouncing the politics of the centre, telling me I should not be in the Labour party.

rows.source: Ma nke a abụghị naanị m.
rows.output: But this is not just about me.
rows.reference: And that is not just my experience.

rows.source: N’ezie, ama m na m ka nwee ihu ọma karịa ụfọdụ ndị ọrụ ibe m n’ihi asịsa ndị ezitere m na abụkarị maka ndọrọndọrọ.
rows.output: Of course, I know I have a better face than some of my colleagues because I am always sent on errands and are usually for political reasons.
rows.reference: Indeed, I know I am more fortunate than some of my colleagues as the comments directed at me tend to be political.

rows.source: Enwere m ntụmanya n’arụmọrụ na mkpebi nke ndị ọrụ ibe m ndị ahụ na enweta nkatọ okike mmadụ ma ọ bụ agbụrụ ya kwa ụbọchị mana ha anaghị agba ọsọ.
rows.output: I have high expectations for the work and decisions of my colleagues, who are constantly receiving criticism of their race or gender, but they do not run away.
rows.reference: I am in awe of the professionalism and determination of those colleagues who face a torrent of sexist or racist abuse every day but never shy away.

rows.source: Otu n’ime akụkụ kachasị ada mmụọ nke oge ndọrọndọrọ a bụ otu okwu nkatọ ndị jọrọ njọ si buru ihe nkịtị.
rows.output: One of the most depressing aspects of this era is how harsh criticism is often taken too seriously.
rows.reference: One of the most disappointing aspects of this era of politics is how levels of abuse have become normalised.

rows.source: Jeremy Corbyn na arịọ n’izu gara aga na ndọrọndọrọ Labour kwesịrị ịmụta omume nke ndidi.
rows.output: Jeremy Corbyn na-arịọ n'izu gara aga na ndọrọndọrọ Labour kwesịrị ịmụta omume nke ndidi.
rows.reference: Jeremy Corbyn claimed last week that the Labour party should foster a culture of tolerance.

rows.source: Eziokwu bụ na anyị abụghịzị ụka ahụ gbasara agbasa, kwa ụkpụrụ “enweghị ntụkwasị obi” ọ bụla ma ọ bụ mgbanwe nke iwu nhọrọ, ndọrọndọrọ ahụ na akpụkọkwa akpụkọ.
rows.output: The truth is that we are not the church that is all about expansion, and we are not about any "trust" policy or change in the selection process, the party, and the media.
rows.reference: The reality is we are no longer that broad church and with every "no-confidence" motion or change of selection rules the party becomes narrower.

rows.source: Enwere m ọtụtụ ndụmọdụ n’ofe afọ abụọ gara aga na agwa m ka m owe isi n’ala, ịhapụ ikwu oke okwu mgbe ahụ ‘m agaghị enwe nsogbu.”
rows.output: I've had a lot of advice over the past two years to get my head out of the sand, to stop talking so much and just 'get on with it.'
rows.reference: I have had lots of advice over the past two years urging me to keep my head down, not to be so vocal and then I would "be all right."

rows.source: Mana nke ahụ abụghị ihe m banyere ndọrọndọrọ ọchịchị ịme.
rows.output: But that's not what I'm about in politics.
rows.reference: But that is not what I came into politics to do.

rows.source: Kemgbe m sonyere Labour afọ 32 ka nwa akwụkwọ, nke nlegharị anya gọọmentị Thatcher kpalitere, nke hapụrụ ime ụlọ akwụkwọ m na nnukwu mmebi, achọrọ m na mbụ idu ọrụ mara mma nke ọhaneze maka ndị kachasị chọọ ha - ma abụ m onye ndu obere mpaghara ma ọ bụ minista gọọmentị.
rows.output: Since I joined Labour 32 years ago as a student, the Thatcher government's policies of cuts have left my school in a state of disrepair, I initially wanted to lead a public service that was a model for those who needed it most - and I was a local leader or a government minister.
rows.reference: Ever since I joined Labour 32 years ago as a school pupil, provoked by the Thatcher government's neglect that had left my comprehensive school classroom literally falling down, I've sought to champion better public services for those who need them most - whether as a local councillor or government minister.

rows.source: Ezobeghị m ndọrọndọrọ ọchịchị m na mbụ, gụnyere ntuli aka ikpeazụ.
rows.output: I have not been involved in politics before, including the last election.
rows.reference: I have never hidden my politics, including at the last election.

rows.source: Ọnweghị onye ọ bụla nọ na Nottingham East ga-enwe mgbagwoju anya gbasara ọnọdụ iwu m yana mpaghara ndị mụ ekwenyeghị n’ọchịchị dị ugbu a.
rows.output: No one in Nottingham East should be confused about my legal situation and the areas I do not agree with the current government.
rows.reference: No one in Nottingham East could have been in any way confused about my policy positions and areas of disagreement with the current leadership.

rows.source: Maka ndị ahụ kwadoro ụkpụrụ ahụ na Fraịde, ihe niile m nwere ike ikwu bụ na mgbe obodo na aga ịnwe Brexit ga-enwe mmetụta adịghị mma n’ọtụtụ ezinụlọ, azụmahịa na ọrụ ọhaneze anyị, aghọtaghị m agụụ iji gbuo oge na ike maka nkwado m na ndị isi ndọrọndọrọ Labour.
rows.output: For those who supported the motion on Friday, all I can say is that when the country goes for Brexit, it will have a negative impact on many families, businesses, and public services, and I don't understand the hunger to waste time and energy in supporting me and the Labour leadership.
rows.reference: To those who promoted the motion on Friday, all I would say is that when the country is ploughing towards a Brexit that will hurt households, businesses and our public services, I do not understand the desire to waste time and energy on my loyalty to the Labour party leader.

rows.source: Mana n’eziokwu otu ozi m nwere abụghị maka Nottingham Momentum, ọ bụ maka ndị mmebe m, ma ọ bụ ndị otu Labour ma ha abụghị: Enwere m afọ ojuju ijere unu ozi ma na ekwe nkwa na ọnweghị ihe egwu mwepu ole ma ọ bụ ngwangwa ndọrọndọrọ ga-akwụsị m ịme ihe m kwere kachasị dịịrị unu niile mma.
rows.output: But one thing I want to make clear is that it's not about Nottingham Momentum, it's about my makers, or the Labour Party if they are not: I am satisfied to serve you and I am committed to not let any risk of expulsion or any other disciplinary measure stop me from doing what I believe is best for all of you.
rows.reference: But really the one message I have is not to Nottingham Momentum, it is to my constituents, whether Labour members or not: I am proud to serve you and I promise that no amount of deselection threats or political expediency will deter me from acting in what I believe are the best interests of you all.

rows.source: Ụlọ akwụkwọ nnwere onwe nke Scotland dowere ndekọ nzọụkwụ nke agụmakwụkwọ kachasị, ma nke a gara n’ihu na 2018 site na iji nsonaazụ ule ndị mara oke mma, nke a na agụzogide site na mmeri ndị mmadụ na ndị otu n’egwuregwu, nka, egwu na mbọ ogbe ndị ọzọ.
rows.output: The Independent Schools of Scotland established a record of excellence in education, which continued in 2018 by using outstanding examination results, which were resisted by the people and the teams in sports, arts, music, and other efforts.
rows.reference: Scotland's independent schools maintain a track record of academic excellence, and this has continued in 2018 with another set of outstanding exam results, which is only strengthened by individual and collective success in sports, art, music and other community endeavours.

rows.source: Na mgbago ọnụọgụ nke ụmụ akwụkwọ 30,000 n’ofe Scotland, ụlọ akwụkwọ ndị a, nke The Scottish Council of Independent Schools (SCIS) na anọchite, na agba mbọ iwete ọkwa ọrụ kachasị maka ụmụ akwụkwọ ha na ndị nne na nna ha.
rows.output: With a total of 30,000 students across Scotland, these schools, represented by the Scottish Council of Independent Schools (SCIS), are making a concerted effort to achieve the best possible outcomes for their students and their parents.
rows.reference: With upwards of 30,000 pupils across Scotland, these schools, represented by The Scottish Council of Independent Schools (SCIS), strive to deliver the best level of service to their pupils and parents.

rows.source: Ụlọ akwụkwọ ndị nnwere onwe na agba mbọ ịkwadobe ụmụ akwụkwọ maka agụmakwụkwọ ọdịnihu na nke dị elu, ọrụaka ha họpụtara yana ọnọdụ ha ka ndị amaala ụwa.
rows.output: Independent schools are working to prepare students for future and higher education, the work they have chosen, and their position as global citizens.
rows.reference: Independent schools aim to prepare their pupils for further and higher education, their chosen career and their place as global citizens.

rows.source: Dị ka ngalaba agụmakwụkwọ nwere ike izube ma tinye usoro ọmụmụ nke ụlọ akwụkwọ dị elu, anyị na ahụ asụsụ ọhụụ ka ọ na aga n’ihu ka nke na akpọtụ yana isiokwu nke nhọrọ achọrọ n’ime ụlọ akwụkwọ.
rows.output: As the education sector can plan and implement a curriculum of higher education institutions, we are also seeing a vision of the language as it goes forward as that which is in line with the themes of the desired choices within the schools.

rows.output: Professor Czeisler recommended that students consider wearing a mask when they wanted to sleep, and when they wanted to wake up, and be aware of the consequences of screen time "blue light" injury and LED light, which could disrupt your body's natural sleep cycle, and lead to sleep problems.

rows.reference: The Ibrox side were looking to record their first win on the road since February's 4-1 triumph at St Johnstone, but Gary Holt's team inflicted just Gerrard's second defeat in 18 games as manager to leave his side eight points adrift of runaway Ladbrokes Premiership leaders Hearts.

rows.source: Nyocha Johnny English Strikes Again - buturu ihe nkiri nzuzo ịkpa ọchị Rowan Atkinson
rows.output: Johnny English Strikes Again - a comedy spy film starring Rowan Atkinson

rows.source: Ọ bụ omenala ugbu a ịchọ mkpa Brexit n’ihe nkiri ọhụrụ ọ bụla nwere nribama Britain, na nke a dịka ọ metụtara mmegharị ihe nkiri ịkpa ọchị nke Johnny English - bụ nke ejiri Johnny English malite na 2003, wee laghachikwa azụ na 2011 ka Johnny English Reborn.
rows.output: It is now a tradition to seek the need for Brexit in every new film with a British cast, and this one is no exception as it relates to the Johnny English comedy franchise - which was first introduced with Johnny English in 2003, and then returned in 2011 as Johnny English Reborn.
rows.reference: It's traditional now to look for Brexit significances in any new film with a British slant and that does seem applicable to this revival of the Johnny English action-comedy spoof franchise - which started back in 2003 with Johnny English and spluttered back to life in 2011 with Johnny English Reborn.

rows.source: Ọ pụtara na ihe nkiri njakịrị nke isiokwu otu anyị siri bụrụ ndị iberibe pụtara ihie, bụzi oghere nbufe ahịa ọhụrụ anyị?
rows.output: It appears that the film's comedic theme of our being fragmented is now a new marketing space for us?
rows.reference: Will tongue-in-cheek self-satire on the subject of how obviously rubbish we are be the nation's new export opportunity?

rows.source: Kosiladị, onye nzuzu anya ọkpụ, ihu rọba Johnny English emegharịala ikike ya ịkwalite ihe nke ugboro abụọ - aha ya karịa ihe ọ bụla na-egosi na ọ bụ nchepụta ihe ịkpa ọchị emebere maka akụkụ obodo ndị anaghị asụ Bekee.
rows.output: In addition, the blind fool, the plastic face Johnny English has once again reinvented his ability to promote something - his name more than anything else shows that it is a comedy creation made for the non-English speaking parts of the world.
rows.reference: At any rate, the pop-eyed, rubber-faced incompetent Johnny English has had his licence to cock things up renewed for the second time - that name of his signalling more than anything else that he is a broad comic creation designed for non-English-speaking cinemagoing territories.

rows.source: N’ezie ọ bụ onye iberibe ọrụ nzuzo nke agbanyeghị ṅṅomi ya gbagwojuru anya, nwere obere Clouseau, ntakịrị Mr Bean na nfechalụ nke nwoke ahụ n’etinye otu olu na isiokwu Chariots of Fire na mmalite mmemme Olympics London 2012.
rows.output: Of course, he is a half-baked secret agent whose clumsy mimicry of his idol, Clouseau, is mixed with a dash of Mr. Bean and the awkwardness of a man who, at the beginning of the London 2012 Olympics opening ceremony, mistakenly used one voice for the theme song "Chariots of Fire."
rows.reference: He is of course the daft secret agent who despite his bizarre pretensions to smoothie glamour has got a little bit of Clouseau, a dash of Mr Bean and a dollop of that chap contributing a single note to the Chariots of Fire theme tune at the London 2012 Olympics opening ceremony.

rows.source: N’izizi ọ dabere n’onye njem yana nwoke nzuzo mba ụwa Atkinson nke emere na ihe mgbasa ozi Barclaycard TV echefugoro, na-ahapu ọgbaghara n’azụ ya.
rows.output: At first, you were based on a travel agent and a secret international man Atkinson made in a forgotten Barclaycard TV advertisement, leaving a trail of chaos in his wake.
rows.reference: He's also originally based on the traveller and international man of mystery Atkinson once played in the now forgotten Barclaycard TV ads, leaving chaos in his wake.

rows.source: Enwere otu oge ma ọ bụ abụọ mara mma na JE ọhụrụ a.
rows.output: There is one or two beautiful things in this new JE.
rows.reference: There are one or two nice moments in this latest JE outing.

rows.source: Ọ masịrị m ka Johnny English na-erute nso n’ụgbọ elu ebe oyi uwe agha ndị agba ochie, igwe nkucha were na-akụta n’okpu agha ya.
rows.output: I liked Johnny English getting close to the plane where the old military uniforms, the washing machine drum was beating on his military cap.
rows.reference: I loved Johnny English approaching a helicopter while dressed in a medieval suit of armour and the rotor blades briefly clanging against his helmet.

rows.source: Onyinye Atkinson nwere maka ịkpa ọchị a na-ahụ anya pụtara ihie, mana ịkpa ọchị ahụ esighi ike ma mafee oke, tụmadị ihe nkiri ndị ahụ “anaghị akpa ọchị” dịka 007 na Mission Impossible n’onwe ha na-enwekwa ihe ịkpa ọchị n’ime ya ugbu a.
rows.output: Atkinson's gift for slapstick comedy was evident, but the comedy was not strong enough and went over the top, making the films "not funny" like the 007 and Mission Impossible films on their own, and now also has comedy in it.
rows.reference: Atkinson's gift for physical comedy is on display, but the humour feels pretty underpowered and weirdly superfluous, especially as the "serious" film brands like 007 and Mission Impossible themselves now confidently offer comedy as an ingredient.

rows.source: Ihe ịkpa ọchị ahụ dịka ọ bụ ụmụaka ka emebere ya karịa ndị okenye, maka mụ onwe m njegheri Johnny English enweghị ihe nchepụta pụrụ iche yana ebumnuche ya dịka ihe nkiri anaghị ekwu okwu nke Atkinson, n’onye nke Bean.
rows.output: The humor of the film is more childish than for adults, for my own part, Johnny English's adventures lack originality and purpose as a non-verbal comedy of Atkinson, in whom Bean excels.
rows.reference: The humour feels as if it is pitched at kids rather than adults, and for me Johnny English's wacky misadventures aren't as inventive and focused as Atkinson's silent-movie gags in the persona of Bean.

rows.source: Ebe mgbado ukwu isiokwu ugbu a bụ na Great Britain nọ n’oke nsogbu.
rows.output: The main topic of discussion at the moment is that Great Britain is in a great crisis.
rows.reference: The perennially topical premise now is that Great Britain is in serious trouble.

rows.source: Onye nbanye ịntanetị anataghị ikike banyere na netwọk ndị ọrụ nzuzo kachasị dị nzuzo nke Britain, kpughee ndị ọrụ nzuzo niile nọ n’ọrụ, na mgbagwoju anya onye ọrụ nzuzo nọ ọrụ - obere ihe omume maka Kelvin Eldon.
rows.output: An unauthorized internet user gained access to Britain's most secret intelligence network, revealed all the secret agents at work, and caused confusion among the secret agents - a small incident for Kelvin Eldon.
rows.reference: A cyber-hacker has infiltrated Britain's super-secret web network of spies, revealing the identities of all Britain's agents in the field, to the dismay of the agent on duty - a regrettably small role for Kevin Eldon.

rows.source: Ọ bụ nke ikpeazụ maka onye isi ala bụ onye mpako nwere nsogbu, nke enweghịzi nkwado ọchịchị ọ bụla kpamkpam: Emma Thompson nwara ike ya na ime ihe omume a yitebere Teresa-May mana enwekebeghị ihe dị n’akwụkwọ ọ ga-eji rụọ ọrụ.
rows.output: It was the last for the president who was a proud man, who had no support from any political party: Emma Thompson tried her best in this role that was modeled after Theresa May but there was nothing in the script to work with.
rows.reference: It's the last straw for a prime minister who is a pompous and embattled figure, already suffering a complete meltdown of political unpopularity: Emma Thompson does her very best with this quasi-Teresa-May character but there's nothing much in the script to work with.

rows.source: Ndị na-enye ya ndụmọdụ nchekwa gwara ya na ebe amagoro ndị ọrụ nzuzo ya niile, ọ ga-akpọpụta onye lagoro ezumike nka.

rows.reference: And that means bumbling Johnny English himself, now employed as a schoolmaster in some posh establishment, but giving off-the-record lessons in how to be an undercover operative: some nice gags here, as English offers a School of Rock-type academy of spying.

rows.output: The English and Bough embarked on a journey of their own comedic antics: they transformed into a waiter, they set fire to a French restaurant; they caused a stir by sneaking into a Volta boat; the English caused confusion by trying to use a Virtual Reality headset to make Volta's living room.
rows.reference: English and Bough begin their odyssey of farcical high-jinks: disguised as waiters, they set fire to a flash French restaurant; they create mayhem smuggling themselves aboard Volta's luxury yacht; and English triggers pure anarchy as he attempts to use a Virtual Reality headset to familiarise himself with the interior of Volta's house.

rows.source: Labour na-agọnarị na ha anaghị akpa nkata atụmatụ ka ndị Britain na-arụ ọrụ ụbọchị anọ n’izu ma nara ụgwọ ọrụ maka ụbọchị ise
rows.output: The Labour Party denies that they are planning to force the British to work four days a week and pay for five
rows.reference: Labour denies it is devising a plan for Britons to work a four day week but be paid for five days

rows.source: Labour Party nke Jeremy Corbyn na-atule atụmatụ ga-agbanwe ihe nke ga-ahụ na ndị Britain rụọ ọrụ ụbọchị anọ n’izu ha anara ụgwọ ọrụ maka ụbọchị ise.
rows.output: The Labour Party, led by Jeremy Corbyn, is considering a plan that would see workers in Britain work four days a week and receive pay for five.
rows.reference: Jeremy Corbyn's Labour Party is to consider a radical plan which will see Britons working a four day week - but getting paid for five.

rows.source: Ndị otu a chọrọ ka ndị isi nwe ụlọ ọrụ na-enyefe akụ ha chekwabara n’aka ndị ọrụ siterena mgbanwe artificial intelligence (AI) site na inye ha ụbọchị ụma agaghị arụ ọrụ.
rows.output: This group wants company executives to transfer their accumulated wealth to workers through a siteraena artificial intelligence (AI) change by giving them a day off.
rows.reference: The party reportedly wants company bosses to pass on savings made through the artificial intelligence (AI) revolution to workers by giving them an extra day off.

rows.source: Ọ ga-eme na ndị na-arụ ọrụ ga-erite elele ụbọchị atọ n’izu ụka ma welakwaa otu ụgwọ ọnwa.
rows.output: It will be made that those who work will have three days off in a week and will be paid a full salary.
rows.reference: It would see employees enjoy a three-day weekend - but still take home the same pay.

rows.source: Ndị nzuputa okwu kwuru na echiche a “ga-adaba” na ebumnuche yana atụmatụ akụnụba nke otu a ime ka ọ dabaara ndị ọrụ.
rows.output: The spokespersons of the group said that this idea "will be in line" with the objectives and economic plans of the group to make it more suitable for the workers.
rows.reference: Sources said the idea would 'fit' with the party's economic agenda and plans to tilt the country in favour of workers.

rows.source: Ndị otu Trades Union Congress akwadola ịmalite ụbọchị anọ n’ime izu dịka ụzọ ndị ọrụ ga-esi rite elele na akụnụba na-agbanwe.
rows.output: The Trade Union Congress has endorsed a four-day workweek as a way for workers to cope with the changing economy.
rows.reference: Shifting to a four-day week has been endorsed by the Trades Union Congress as a way for workers to take advantage of the changing economy.

rows.source: Onye senịọ nzuputa okwu nke Labour Party gwara Sunday Times: ‘A na-atu anya ịma ọkwa nyocha amụma tupu ngwucha afọ a.
rows.output: The Labour Party's spokesperson for foreign affairs told the Sunday Times: 'We are looking to make an announcement on the policy review before the end of the year.
rows.reference: A senior Labour Party source told The Sunday Times: 'A policy review is expected to be announced before the end of the year.

rows.source: ‘Ọ gaghị eme ozugbo mana ịrụ ọrụ ụbọchị anọ n’izu bụ ebumnobi ndị otu a dabara n’usoro ihazi akụnụba ka ọ dabaara ndị ọrụ yana mkpokota ụzọ nrụpụta ihe nke ndị otu ahụ.’
rows.output: 'It won't be immediate, but working four days a week is the goal of this group, which is in line with the economic planning of the group, to benefit the workers and the overall production capacity of the group.'
rows.reference: 'It won't happen overnight but a four-day working week is an aspiration that fits in with the party's approach to rebalancing the economy in favour of the worker as well as the party's overall industrial strategy.'

rows.source: Labour Party agaghị abụ ndị izizi kwadoro echiche a, ebe Green Party kwere nkwa ịrụ ọrụ ụbọchị anọ n’izu n’ime oge ndọrọndọrọ ọchịchị 2017.
rows.output: The Labour Party will not be the first to support this idea, while the Green Party has promised to work four days a week during the 2017 election period.
rows.reference: The Labour Party would not be the first to endorse such an idea, with the Green Party pledging a four-day working week during its 2017 general election campaign.

rows.source: Labour Party anaghị akwado ebumnuche ahụ ugbu a dịka otu, kosiladị.
rows.output: The Labour Party does not currently support the objective as a party, especially.
rows.reference: The aspiration is currently not being endorsed by the Labour Party as a whole, however.

rows.source: Onye nkwuchite okwu Labour Party kwuru: ‘Ọrụ ụbọchị anọ n’izu abughị amụma ndị otu a nke na ndị otu a anaghị atule ya.’
rows.output: The Labour Party spokesperson said: 'The four-day workweek is not a policy that this group of members is considering.'
rows.reference: A Labour Party spokesman said: 'A four-day working week is not party policy and it is not being considered by the party.'

rows.source: Shadow Chancellor John McDonnell jiri ọgbakọ Labour mere izu gara aga were kọwapụta echiche ya maka mgbanwe na akụnụba.
rows.output: Shadow Chancellor John McDonnell used the Labour Party conference last week to outline his ideas for transforming the economy.
rows.reference: Shadow Chancellor John McDonnell used last week's Labour conference to flesh out his vision for a socialist revolution in the economy.

rows.source: Mazị McDonnell kwuru na o kpebiri iweghachite ikike site na n’aka ndị ‘isi ụlọ ọrụ amaghị’ yana “ndị nrite oke uru’ n’ụlọ ọrụ ndị eji ebi ndụ.
rows.output: Mr. McDonnell said he decided to restore the right to strike from "unknown corporate executives" and "excessive profit recipients" in essential services companies.
rows.reference: Mr McDonnell said he was determined to claw back power from 'faceless directors' and 'profiteers' at utility firms.

rows.source: Atụmatụ shadow chancellor ahụ pụtakwara na ndị nwere oke n’ụlọ ọrụ mmiri nwere ike ha agaghị enwetacha isi ego ha, maka gọọmentị Labour nwere ike ‘ime mwepu’ na ndabere ebumnobi ihe ezighi ezi.
rows.output: The shadow chancellor's plan also means that those who are well off in the water industry may not get the full amount of profit they expect, because the Labour government may 'cut back' on the basis of incorrect target assumptions.
rows.reference: The shadow chancellor's plans also mean current shareholders in water companies may not get back their entire stake as a Labour government could make 'deductions' on the grounds of perceived wrongdoing.

rows.source: O kwuputakwara atụmatụ itinye ndị ọrụ na bọdụ ụlọ ọrụ ma mepụta Inclusive Ownership Fund ga-enyefe pesenti 10 n’oke ụlọ ọrụ ndị nkịtị n’aka ndị ọrụ, ndị nwere ike inweta uru isi ego ruru £500.
rows.output: He also announced plans to put workers on the boards of companies and create an Inclusive Ownership Fund that would transfer up to 10 percent of the shares of publicly traded companies to workers, who could benefit from a maximum of £500 in equity.
rows.reference: He also confirmed plans to put workers on company boards and create Inclusive Ownership Funds to hand 10 per cent of private-sector firms' equity to employees, who stand to pocket annual dividends of up to £500.

rows.reference: While it is normal for foreign governments to place advertisements to promote trade, Beijing and Washington are currently locked in an escalating trade war that has seen them level rounds of tariffs on each other's imports.

rows.source: Ntinye ụtụ ngwahịa nke China mere na mbido agha azụmahịa ka emebere ka ọ metụta ndị na ebupu ahịa n’obodo dịka Iowa kwadoro otu ndọrọndọrọ Repọblikan nke Trump, ndị ọkammara China na U.S kwuru.
rows.output: The Chinese government's introduction of tariffs in the early stages of the trade war was designed to target exporters from states like Iowa that supported a Republican president, Trump, Chinese officials and U.S. officials said.
rows.reference: China's retaliatory tariffs early in the trade war were designed to hit exporters in states such as Iowa that supported Trump's Republican Party, Chinese and U.S. experts have said.

rows.source: Terry Branstad, onye nnọchite anya U.S na China bụkwa onye chịburu Iowa, onye mbupu ahịa nri ubi nke ukwuu na China, kwuru na China merụrụ ndị ọrụ, ndị ọrụ ugbo na azụmahịa nke America ahụ.
rows.output: Terry Branstad, the U.S. Trade Representative to China and former governor of Iowa, which is a major agricultural exporter to China, said that China has harmed American workers, farmers, and businesses.
rows.reference: Terry Branstad, the U.S. ambassador to China and the former longtime governor of Iowa, a major exporter of agricultural goods to China, said Beijing had hurt American workers, farmers and businesses.

rows.source: China, Branstad dere n’echiche ya na Des Moines Register na Sọnde, “na-ekwusi ike maka mmegide ahụ site na itinye mgbasa ozi n’akwụkwọ mgbasa ozi anyị.”
rows.output: China, Branstad wrote in his column in the Des Moines Register on Sunday, "emphasizes the opposition by putting advertising in our newspapers."
rows.reference: China, Branstad wrote in an opinion piece in Sunday's Des Moines Register, "is now doubling down on that bullying by running propaganda ads in our own free press."

rows.source: “N’ịgbasa ozi asị a, gọọmentị China na ewere oghere omenala America hụrụ n’anya bụ nke onye kwuo uche ya na mgbasa ozi enweghị mkpagbu were tinye mgbasa ozi akwụrụ ụgwọ na Des Moines Register.” Branstad dere.
rows.output: "In spreading this message, the Chinese government has taken advantage of the cherished American tradition of free speech and the press, which is protected by our Constitution, and has inserted paid advertising in the Des Moines Register." Branstad wrote.
rows.reference: "In disseminating its propaganda, China's government is availing itself of America's cherished tradition of free speech and a free press by placing a paid advertisement in the Des Moines Register," Branstad wrote.

rows.source: “Ma ịtụlee ya n’ọdụ akwụkwọ mgbasa ozi dị n’okporo beijing ebe a, ịga ahụ na enwere obere olu ndịiche nke na ịghaghị ahụ ihe n’egosi n’ezie echiche di iche ndị China nwere ike nwee maka usoro akụnụba China nọ na nsogbu, ebe ọ bụ n’ụlọ mgbasa ozi nọ na njikwa nke China Communist Party,” ọ dere.
rows.output: "But when you look at the media outlets in Beijing, you can see that there is a small number of dissenting voices that you have to look at to really understand the different views that the Chinese people may have about the Chinese economic system, which is in trouble, because the media is under the control of the Chinese Communist Party," he wrote.
rows.reference: "In contrast, at the newsstand down the street here in Beijing, you will find limited dissenting voices and will not see any true reflection of the disparate opinions that the Chinese people may have on China's troubling economic trajectory, given that media is under the firm thumb of the Chinese Communist Party," he wrote.

rows.source: Ọ gbakwunyere na “otu n’ime akwụkwọ akụkọ ama ama na China zenarịrị ibiputa” ederede ya, n’agbanyeghị na o kwughị akwụkwọ akụkọ nke ọ bụ.
rows.output: He also added that "one of the most famous Chinese novels that has escaped censorship" was his, although he did not mention the novel.
rows.reference: He added that "one of China's most prominent newspapers dodged the offer to publish" his article, although he did not say which newspaper.

rows.source: Ndị Repọblikan Na-akpachapụ Ndị Ntuli Aka Ụmụ-nwanyị Tupu Ntuli Aka Ọkara Ọchịchị Maka Ọgbaghara Kavanaugh, Ndị Nyocha Dọrọ Aka na Ntị
rows.output: The Republican Party is trying to suppress the votes of women before the midterm elections, and the investigations are being used to distract from the controversy of Kavanaugh.
rows.reference: Republicans Alienating Women Voters Ahead of Midterms With Kavanaugh Debacle, Analysts Warn

rows.source: Dị ka ọtụtụ ndị isi Repọblikan kwụnyere ma kwuchitere Onye nhọpụta Ụlọ Ikpe Kachasị Elu Brett Kavanaugh n’ihu ebubo dị iche iche nke mmekọrịta nwoke na nwanyị, ndị nyocha adọọla aka na ntị na ha ga-ahụ ndapụta iwe ga-esite ọkachasị n’aka ụmụ-nwanyị, n’oge ntuli aka ọkara ọchịchị na-abịa.
rows.output: Like many Republican leaders, the nominee to the Supreme Court, Brett Kavanaugh, has been accused of sexual misconduct, and investigators have warned that the most passionate opposition to his confirmation will come from women, in the upcoming midterm elections.
rows.reference: As many top Republicans stand-by and defend Supreme Court nominee Brett Kavanaugh in the face of several allegations of sexual assault, analyst have warned they will see a backlash, particularly from women, during the upcoming midterm elections.

rows.source: Mmetụta sochiri nke a dị elu nke ukwuu, na ọtụtụ ndị Repọblikan ka edekọbara na ha egosila na ha chọrọ ịga n’ihu mee ntuli aka.
rows.output: The consequences of this are so severe that many Republicans have been recorded as saying that they want to go ahead and hold an election.
rows.reference: The emotions surrounding this have been extremely high, and most Republicans are on record already showing they wanted to go forward with a vote.

rows.source: Enweghị ike iweghachi ihe ndị ahụ,” Grant Reeher, onye ọkammụta nke sayensị ndọrọndọrọ ọchịchị na Syracuse University Maxwell School gwara The Hill maka ederede nke ebiputara na Satọde.
rows.output: "Nothing can be done to restore the trust," Grant Reeher, a professor of political science at Syracuse University's Maxwell School told The Hill in a written statement on Saturday.
rows.reference: Those things can't be walked back," Grant Reeher, a professor of political science at Syracuse University's Maxwell School told The Hill for an article published Saturday.

rows.source: Reeher kwuru na ya na-agbagha n’ọkwụkwa ikpeazụ nke Onye Ọmebe Iwu Jeff Flake (R-Arizona) mere maka nyocha FBI a ga-ezu iji wetuo iwe ndị ntuli aka.
rows.output: Reeher said he was disappointed in the last-minute amendment by Senator Jeff Flake (R-Arizona) for the FBI investigation to be conducted to appease the voters.
rows.reference: Reeher said he doubts Senator Jeff Flake's (R-Arizona) last-minute push for an FBI investigation will be enough to placate angry voters.

rows.source: “Ụmụ-nwanyị agaghị echefu ihe mere ụnyahụ - ha agaghị echefu echi niile ma Nọvemba, “ Karine Jean-Pierre, onye ndụmọdụ senịọ na onye nkwuchite okwu obodo maka otu ọganihu MoveOn kwuru na Fraịde, dabere na akwụkwọ akụkọ Washington, D.C.
rows.output: "Women will not forget what happened yesterday - they will not forget tomorrow and November," Karine Jean-Pierre, a senior adviser and spokesperson for the progressive group MoveOn, said on Friday, according to the Washington Post.
rows.reference: "Women are not going to forget what happened yesterday - they are not going to forget it tomorrow and not in November," Karine Jean-Pierre, a senior adviser and national spokeswoman for the progressive group MoveOn said on Friday, according to the Washington, D.C. newspaper.

rows.source: N’ụtụtụ Fraịde, ndị ngagharị iwe kwere ukwe “Nọvemba na-abịa!” ka ha na-agagharị ngagharị iwe n’ogologo ụzọ Nzụkọ Ọmeiwu ebe ndị Repọblikan ji Ọgbakọ Ọka Ikpe họrọ ịga n’ihu na nhọrọ Kavanaugh agbanyeghị nkwuputa Dr. Christine Blasey Ford, Mic kwuputara.
rows.output: On Friday morning, protesters chanted "November is coming!" as they marched through the streets of the Capitol Hill neighborhood where Republicans decided to proceed with the confirmation of Supreme Court nominee Brett Kavanaugh despite the testimony of Dr. Christine Blasey Ford, Mic reported.
rows.reference: On Friday morning, protestors chanted "November is coming!" as they demonstrated in the hallway of the Senate as the Republicans controlling the Judiciary Committee chose to move forward with Kavanaugh's nomination despite the testimony of Dr. Christine Blasey Ford, Mic reported.

rows.source: “Ịnụ ọkụ n’obi na mkpalite mmụọ nke Demokrat ga-apụ iche,” Stu Rothenberg, onye nyocha ndọrọndọrọ ọchịchị enweghị otu o binyere gwara ndị akụkọ.
rows.output: "Enthusiasm and momentum of the Democrats will be different," Stu Rothenberg, a nonpartisan political analyst, told reporters.
rows.reference: "Democratic enthusiasm and motivation is going to be off the chart," Stu Rothenberg, a nonpartisan political analyst, told the news site.

rows.source: “Ndị mmadụ na-ekwu na ọ dịla elu; nke a bụ eziokwu.
rows.output: "People say that it's high; this is true."
rows.reference: "People are saying it's already been high; that's true.

rows.source: Mana ọ nwere ike ịgbagokwu ọkachasị n’etiti ụmụ-nwanyị n’enweghị otu ha binyere n’ime obodo yana ndị ntuli aka na-etolite etolite, gbara afọ 18- ruo 29-, bụ ndị ebe onye isi ala anaghị amasị, anaghị eme ntuli aka kwa mgbe.”
rows.output: But you can also see the greatest growth among women who are not registered in the community and among young voters, aged 18 to 29, who are not fond of the president and do not vote regularly.
rows.reference: But it could be higher, particularly among swing women voters in the suburbs and younger voters, 18- to 29-year-olds, who while they don't like the president, often don't vote."

rows.source: Ọbụlagodi tupu nkwuputanke ọha Ford mere na-akọwa ebubo mmekọrịta nwoke na nwanyị megide onye nhọpụta Ụlọ Ikpe kachasị Elu, ndị nyocha na-atụ elo na ndapụta iwe nwere ike sote ma ọ bụrụ na ndị Repọblikan gaa n’ihu mee nkwado ahụ.
rows.output: Even before Ford's public statement, investigators were suggesting that a backlash could follow if Republicans proceeded with the endorsement.
rows.reference: Even before Ford's public testimony detailing her allegations of sexual assault against the Supreme Court nominee, analysts suggested a backlash could follow if Republicans pushed forward with the confirmation.

rows.source: “Nke a abụrụla ọgbaghara dịịrị GOP,” Michael Steele kwuru, onye isi chịburu Ọgbakọ Otu Repọblikan, na mbido izug ara aga, dabere na NBC News.
rows.output: "This has become a nightmare for the GOP," said Michael Steele, the former chairman of the Republican National Committee, on the first day of the week, based on NBC News.
rows.reference: "This has become a muddled mess for the GOP," said Michael Steele, former chairman of the Republican National Committee, early last week, according to NBC News.

rows.source: “Ọ bụghị naanị maka ntuli aka ndị ọgbakọ ma ọ bụ maka ntuli aka ikpeazụ ma ọ bụ ma etinyere Kavanaugh n’oche, ọ bụkwa maka otu ndị Repọblikan siri jikwaa ihe a ma ka ha siri meso ya omume,” Guy Cecil, onye isi Priorities USA, otu na-enyere aka ahọpụta ndị Demokrat, rụtụrụ ndị akụkọ aka.
rows.output: "It's not just about the primaries or the general election, but also about how the Republicans are handling this and how they are going to act on it," Guy Cecil, the president of Priorities USA, a Democratic group, told reporters.
rows.reference: "It's just not about the committee vote or the final vote or whether Kavanaugh is put on the bench, it's also about the way Republicans have handled this and how they have treated her," Guy Cecil, director of Priorities USA, a group that helps to elect Democrats, pointed out to the news channel.

rows.source: Kaosiladị, Ndị America dị ka ndị kewara ekewa n’onye ha ga-ekwenyere na ndapụta nkwuputa Ford na Kavanaugh, ebe ndị karịrị kwụnyere onye nke ikpeazụ.
rows.output: However, Americans are as divided as they were on whom to trust Ford's and Kavanaugh's statements, where more than half sided with the latter.
rows.reference: However, Americans appear to be somewhat split over who to believe in the wake of Ford's and Kavanaugh's testimonies, with slightly more siding with the latter.

rows.source: Nyocha ọhụrụ sitere na YouGov gosiri na pesentị 41 ndị zara ajụjụ kwenyere kpamkpam ma ọ bụ kwenyetụrụ nkwuputa Ford, ebe pesentị 35 kwuru na ha kwenyere kpamkpam ma ọ bụ kwenyetụrụ Kavanaugh.
rows.output: A recent survey from YouGov showed that 41% of respondents agreed or strongly agreed with Ford's statements, while 35% agreed or strongly agreed with Kavanaugh's statements.
rows.reference: A new poll from YouGov shows that 41 percent of respondents definitely or probably believed Ford's testimony, while 35 percent said they definitely or probably believed Kavanaugh.

rows.source: Na mgbakwunye, pesentị 38 kwuru na ha chere na Kavanaugh eleghị anya sịrị asị ma ọ bụ sịa asị kpamkpam n’oge nkwuputa ya, ebe naanị pesentị 30 kwuru otu ihe ahụ maka Ford.
rows.output: Furthermore, 38 percent said they believed that Kavanaugh was probably lying or completely lying during his testimony, while only 30 percent said the same about Ford.
rows.reference: Additionally, 38 percent said they thought Kavanaugh has probably or definitely lied during his testimony, while just 30 percent said the same about Ford.

rows.source: Ka Flake mechara nkwanye, ndị FBI na-eme nyocha ugbu a n’ebubo Ford boro, yana opekempe otu onye ebubo ọzọ, Deborah Ramirez mere, The Guardian kwuputara.
rows.output: After Flake's resignation, the FBI is currently investigating Ford's allegations, with at least one other allegation, made by Deborah Ramirez, reported by The Guardian.
rows.reference: After the push from Flake, the FBI is currently investigating the allegations brought forward by Ford as well as at least one other accuser, Deborah Ramirez, The Guardian reported.

rows.source: Ford mere nkwuputa n’ihu Ọgbakọ Ndị Ikpe Nzụkọ Ọmeiwu n’okpuru iyi n’izu gara aga na Kavanaugh dakporo ya n’anya mmanya mgbe ọ gbara afọ 17.
rows.output: Ford made a statement before the Senate Judiciary Committee last week that Kavanaugh assaulted her when she was 17 years old.
rows.reference: Ford testified before the Senate Judiciary Committee under oath last week that Kavanaugh drunkenly assaulted her at the age of 17.

rows.source: Ramirez boro ebubo n’onye nhọpụta Ụlọ Ikpe Kachasị Elu ahụ gosiri ya ike ya mgbe ha na-eme ọgbakọ oriri na ọṅụṅụ n’oge ha na-agụ akwụkwọ na Yale n’ime 1980s.
rows.output: Ramirez accused the Supreme Court nominee of showing off his wealth during social gatherings during their time at Yale Law School in the 1980s.
rows.reference: Ramirez alleges that the Supreme Court nominee exposed his genitals to her while they attended a party during their time studying at Yale in the 1980s.

rows.source: Onye Mmepụta World Wide Web Na-ama Atụmatụ Ịmalite Ịntanetị Ọhụrụ Iji Sonyere Google na Facebook
rows.output: The World Wide Web inventor is planning to launch a new Internet to compete with Google and Facebook
rows.reference: The Inventor of the World Wide Web Plans to Start a New Internet to Take on Google and Facebook

rows.source: Tim Berners-Lee, onye mmepụta World Wide Web, na-amalite ụlọ ọrụ ọhụrụ nke ga-achụso Facebook, Amazon na Google.
rows.output: Tim Berners-Lee, the inventor of the World Wide Web, is starting a new company that will compete with Facebook, Amazon, and Google.
rows.reference: Tim Berners-Lee, the inventor of the World Wide Web, is launching a startup that seeks to rival Facebook, Amazon and Google.

rows.source: Atụmatụ ọhụrụ ahụ nke ọkaibe teknụzụ, Inrupt, bụ ụlọ ọrụ na-agbakwasa ụkwụ na ngwanro ghe oghe Berners-Lee, Solid.
rows.output: The new plan, Inrupt, is a tech startup that is disrupting the open-source software landscape created by Berners-Lee, Solid.
rows.reference: The technology legend's latest project, Inrupt, is a company that builds off of Berners-Lee's open source platform Solid.

rows.source: Solid na-enye ndị ọrụ oghere ịhọrọ ebe ha ga-echekwa data ha yana ozi ndị mmadụ nwere ike nweta.
rows.output: Solid provides users with the flexibility to choose where they want to store their data and information that people can access.
rows.reference: Solid allows users to choose where their data is stored and what people are allowed to have access to what information.

rows.source: N’ajụjụ ọnụ pụrụ iche Fast Company mere, Berners-Lee mara njakịrị na ebumnuche ejiri mebe Inrupt bụ “ịchị mba ụwa.”
rows.output: In a special interview with Fast Company, Berners-Lee joked that the purpose of Inrupt was "to rule the world."
rows.reference: In an exclusive interview with Fast Company, Berners-Lee joked that the intent behind Inrupt is "world domination."

rows.source: “Anyị ga-eme ya ugbu a,” o kwuru maka ụlọ ọhụrụ ahụ.
rows.output: "We will do it now," he said for the new house.
rows.reference: "We have to do it now," he said of the startup.

rows.source: “Ọ bụ oge a ga-edebanye na akụkọ.”
rows.output: "It's time to register for the program."
rows.reference: "It's a historical moment."

rows.source: Ngwa ahụ na-eji teknụzụ Solid enye ndị mmadụ oghere imepụta “ebe nchekwa data nkeonwe n’ịntanetị” ma ọ bụ POD.
rows.output: The device uses Solid technology to give people the opportunity to create their own "personal online data storage" or POD.
rows.reference: The app uses Solid's technology to allow people to create their own "personal online data store" or a POD.

rows.source: Ọ nwere ike inwe ndepụta kọntaktị, ndepụta ihe omume, kalenda, ọba egwu yana ngwa nkeonwe na nke eji arụ ọrụ.
rows.output: It may have a contact list, a to-do list, a calendar, a music library, and personal and work apps.
rows.reference: It can contain contact lists, to-do lists, calendar, music library and other personal and professional tools.

rows.source: Ọ dị ka Google Drive, Microsoft Outlook, Slack na Spotify dị n’otu nchọgharị ma ha niile n’otu oge.
rows.output: It's like Google Drive, Microsoft Outlook, Slack, and Spotify all in one browser and all at once.
rows.reference: It's like Google Drive, Microsoft Outlook, Slack and Spotify are all available on one browser and all at the same time.

rows.source: Ihe pụrụ iche na ebe nchekwa data nkeonwe n’ịntanetị bụ na ọ dịịrị naanị onye ji ya arụ ọrụ ịhọrọ onye ga-enweta ozi nke ọ bụla.
rows.output: The unique thing about a personal online database is that it is up to the person who owns it to decide who gets to access the information.
rows.reference: What's unique about the personal online data store is that it is completely up to the user who can access what kind of information.

rows.source: Ụlọ ọrụ ahụ na-akpọ ya “ikike nkeonwe site na data.”
rows.output: The company calls it "personalization by data."
rows.reference: The company calls it "personal empowerment through data."

rows.source: Ebumnuche Inrupt, dabere na CEO John Bruce, bụ ka ụlọ ọrụ kpokọba, akụrụngwa, usoro na nka dabara daba iji nyere aka mee ka Solid rute onye ọ bụla.
rows.output: The mission of Inrupt, based on CEO John Bruce, is to aggregate, equip, enable, and empower individuals to make Solid accessible to everyone.
rows.reference: The idea for Inrupt, according to the company's CEO John Bruce, is for the company to bring resources, process and appropriate skills to help make Solid available to everyone.

rows.source: Ụlọ ọrụ ahụ nwere naanị Berners-Lee, Bruce, ebe nchekwa IBM zụtara na ya, ndị ọrụ nrụpụta ewere n’ọrụ ịrụ n’atụmatụ ahụ yana ọgbakọ ndị koodu wepụtara onwe ha.
rows.output: The company was only Berners-Lee, Bruce, where IBM's storage division had purchased, and a team of engineers hired to work on the project, and a group of volunteer coders who released their own software.
rows.reference: The company currently consists of Berners-Lee, Bruce, a security platform bought by IBM, some on-staff developers contracted to work on the project, and a community of volunteer coders.

rows.source: Site n’izu a, ndị nrụpụta teknụzụ ụwa gbaa gburugburu ga-enwe ike mebe ngwa agaghị ekpokọba ọnụ nke ha site n’iji ngwa mebere na websaịtị Inrupt.
rows.output: By the end of the week, global tech creators will be able to build non-invasive apps of their own using the Inrupt app builder on the website.
rows.reference: Starting this week, technology developers around the world could create their own decentralized apps using the tools available on the Inrupt website.

rows.source: Berners-Lee kwuru na ya ndị otu ya anaghị agwa ndị “Facebook na Google okwu banyere ma ha a ga-amalite ma ọ bụ hapụ mmalite mgbanwe kpamkpam ebe ụdịdị azụmahịa na-atụgharị ozugbo na ntabi anya.
rows.output: Berners-Lee said that his team did not talk to "Facebook and Google" about whether they would start or abandon the radical change where the business model would be turned upside down with the full attention of the media.
rows.reference: Berners-Lee said that he and his team are not talking to "Facebook and Google about whether or not to introduce a complete change where all their business models are completely upended overnight.

rows.source: “Anyị anaghị anata ha ikike.”
rows.output: "We do not accept them."
rows.reference: "We are not asking their permission."

rows.source: Na mbipụta emere na Medium na Satọde, Berners-Lee dere na “ebumnuche Inrupt bụ inye ike azụmahịa na gburugburu inyere aka chekwaa ntụkwasị obi na ịdị mma weebu ọhụrụ ahụ arụrụ na Solid.”
rows.output: In a Medium post published on Saturday, Berners-Lee wrote that "the purpose of Inrupt is to empower businesses to help keep the trust and integrity of the new web that is being built on Solid."
rows.reference: In a post on Medium published on Saturday, Berners-Lee wrote that Inrupt's "mission is to provide commercial energy and an ecosystem to help protect the integrity and quality of the new web built on Solid."

rows.source: Na 1994, Berners-Lee gbanwere Ịntanetị mgbe ọ mepụtara World Wide Web Consortuim na Massachusetts Institue of Technology.
rows.output: In 1994, Berners-Lee revolutionized the Internet by creating the World Wide Web Consortium at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology.
rows.reference: In 1994, Berners-Lee transformed the Internet when he established the World Wide Web Consortium at Massachusetts Institute of Technology.

rows.source: N’ọnwa ndị adịbeghị anya, Berners-Lee bụ olu na-ada ụda na arụmarụ ụka nnwere onwe ọrụ ịntanetị.
rows.output: In recent months, Berners-Lee has been a vocal advocate for the freedom of the internet.
rows.reference: In recent months, Berners-Lee has been an influential voice in the net neutrality debate.

rows.source: Ọbulagodi mgbe a na-ebuputa Inrupt, Berners-Lee ga-anọrọ dịka onye Mmepụta na Onye Isi nke World Wide Web Consortuim, Web Foundation na Open Data Institute.
rows.output: Even when he was leaving the W3C, Berners-Lee would remain as the Founder and Chairman of the World Wide Web Consortium, Web Foundation, and Open Data Institute.
rows.reference: Even while launching Inrupt, Berners-Lee will remain the Founder and Director of World Wide Web Consortium, the Web Foundation and the Open Data Institute.

rows.source: “A na m enwe olile anya nke ukwuu maka oge na-abịa n’ihu nke weebu,” Berners-Lee gbakwunyere.
rows.output: "We are very optimistic about the future of the web," added Berners-Lee.
rows.reference: "I'm incredibly optimistic for this next era of the web," Berners-Lee added.

rows.source: Bernard Vann: Emere emume onye ụkọchukwu Victoria Cross WW1
rows.output: Bernard Vann: A ceremony for the Victoria Cross WW1 priest
rows.reference: Bernard Vann: WW1 Victoria Cross cleric celebrated

rows.source: Emeela emume nke naanị ụkọchukwu Church of England nwetara mmeri Victoria Cross n’oge World War One dị ka onye agha n’obodo ya ka afọ gbara 100.
rows.output: A ceremony was held for the only Church of England vicar to win the Victoria Cross in World War One, as a soldier in his home village, 100 years after the war.
rows.reference: The only Church of England cleric to win a Victoria Cross during World War One as a combatant has been celebrated in his hometown 100 years on.

rows.source: Lt Col Ụkọchukwu Bernard Vann nwetara awọdụ na 29, Septemba 1918 na mbuso agha emere na Bellenglise na Lehaucourt.
rows.output: Lt Col Ụkọchukwu Bernard Vann was awarded the Distinguished Service Cross on 29 September 1918 for the attack made on Bellenglise and Lehaucourt.
rows.reference: Lt Col The Reverend Bernard Vann won the award on 29 September 1918 in the attack at Bellenglise and Lehaucourt.

rows.source: Kaosiladị, mgbọ ọkaibe n’ịgba egbe tụrụ ya ka ụbọchị anọ gachara na ọ maghị ncha ncha na etubere ya ugo ndị agha kachasị na Britain.
rows.output: However, a bullet wound in the leg kept him from walking for four days, and he didn't know how to use a handkerchief, as he had been issued with the best military equipment in Britain.
rows.reference: However, he was killed by a sniper four days later and never knew he had won the highest British military honour.

rows.source: Peter Martin, nke ndị ndụmọdụ azụmahịa CGA, nke kpokọrọ ọnụọgụ ahụ, kwuru: “Anyanwụ ka dị yana nsonye England na World Cup toro ogologo ole atụrụ anya pụtara na Julaị sochiri otu usoro ka ọnwa nke Juun gara aga, mgbe ụlọ mmanya rịgoro pasentị 2.8, belụsọ na ndị ụlọ oriri na ọṅụṅụ nwere nnukwu nhịahụ.
rows.output: Peter Martin, from CGA's business advisory group, which compiled the figures, said: "The sun is still shining and England's participation in the World Cup has meant that the trend of the previous month, when pubs rose by 2.8 percent, has continued into July, with a further rise of 2.8 percent, although restaurants have been less affected.
rows.reference: Peter Martin, of business consultancy CGA, which compiled the figures, said: "Continued sunshine and England's longer than expected participation in the World Cup meant July followed a similar pattern to the previous month of June, when pubs were up 2.8 per cent, except that restaurants were hit even harder.

rows.source: Nrịda nke pasentị 1.8 n’azụmahịa ụlọ oriri na ọṅụṅụ na Juun kawanyere njọ na Julai.
rows.output: A decline of 1.8 percent in restaurant sales in June was worse in July.
rows.reference: The fall of 1.8 per cent in restaurant trading in June just got worse in July.
